newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean Q1 GDP up 3.8 pct vs yr-ago - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Chilean Q1 GDP up 3.8 pct vs yr-ago - central bank.

text.p: Chile's gross domestic product rose 3.8 percent in the first quarter of the year over the same period of 1996, reflecting strong exports and steady growth in the economy, the Central Bank said.
Overall spending in the economy slipped 0.3 percent in the first quarter of the year over the same period of 1996, showing Chileans were saving more, the bank said.

"During this period (first quarter), the dynasism of economic activity was based fundamentally on external demand, marking a change with last year's trend in which there was a significant increase in internal spending," said the Central Bank's twice-monthly report.
Exports led GDP growth in the first quarter, said the report.

"External demand showed significant dynamism, higher than in the two previous quarters. Exports of goods and services grew 15.8 percent, with copper exports outstanding, with growth of over 30 percent, as well as manufactured goods," said the report.
Chilean officials expect the economy to grow about 6.5 percent for the year, though many economists say the real figure will probably be closer to seven percent.
Imports showed a "notable moderation in their pace of growth" with respect to the previous quarter, rising 5.1 percent, said the report.
"Imports of consumer goods fell in the first quarter while those of capital goods showed significant growth," it added.
